title: dedicated gpu pool autoscale warmup personal scratchpad
content:
Personal scratchpad — investigating capacity thrash during warmup (dedicated GPU pool)

Summary / problem statement:
- Intermittent incidents where Dedicated GPU pool autoscaler rapidly scales up nodes but pods remain Pending/Init for long enough that the autoscaler scales down again → capacity thrash, elevated cold-start latency for warm requests.
- Symptoms seen during weekend stress test and in customer-prod on 2026-02-22 evening window.
- Affects pools with GPU-type v100-32 / a10g (reported on both).

Quick timeline (observed):
- 2026-02-22 18:07 UTC: sustained request spike (x3 baseline) from hosted workload.
- 18:08: autoscaler triggers +4 nodes; scale events show nodes provisioning in cloud provider (GCP) w/ instance-init in progress.
- 18:10: kubelet on new nodes registers, but pods for serving runtime (model-worker) remain in Init/ContainerCreating for 60–120s.
- 18:12: autoscaler considers recent low utilization and scales down 2 of the new nodes (cooldown misaligned) → pods get stuck/evicted and requests see timeouts.

Commands / logs I ran (raw-ish):
- kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-inference -o wide
  OUTPUT: newly provisioned nodes show Ready after ~90s, kernel+docker up

- kubectl describe pod model-worker-abc -n dedicated
  SNIPPET:
    Events:
      Type     Reason       Age    From               Message
      ----     ------       ----   ----               -------
      Normal   Scheduled    2m     default-scheduler  Successfully assigned dedicated/model-worker-abc to node-xyz
      Normal   Pulling      2m     kubelet            Pulling image "ghcr.io/redwood/model-worker:prod-2026-02-20"
      Normal   Pulled       90s    kubelet            Successfully pulled image
      Warning  FailedSync   80s    kubelet            Error: failed to start container: error while creating device: NVML not initialized

- journalctl -u kubelet on new nodes:
  SNIPPET:
  Feb 22 18:09:07 node-xyz kubelet[...]: failed to attach gpus: NVML: Driver not loaded
  Feb 22 18:09:08 node-xyz kubelet[...]: gpu plugin: waiting for nvidia-device-plugin pods

- kubectl logs nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -n kube-system -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin
  OUTPUT: some init containers crash with: "nvidia-smi returned non-zero exit code" then recover after 30s

- cloud provider provisioning logs (GCP): instance boot time 40s, but custom startup script that installs driver and kubelet plugin takes ~45–60s extra (we ship a post-boot step to ensure driver matchs kernel).

Hypotheses (working):
1) Driver/plugin warmup latency mismatch: instance is Ready but GPU drivers / device plugin not ready → pods transition to ContainerCreating and kubelet reports device errors. Autoscaler sees nodes Ready and counts them toward capacity, but pods can't start using GPUs. When utilization drops slightly, autoscaler scales down again (policy/cooldown short) → thrash.
2) StartupProbe / readinessProbe complexity: our model-worker has readiness that waits for GPU init; on slow nodes it remains unready, and ScaleDown uses different metric (node utilization) and doesn't account for delayed readiness.
3) Image pull + driver install overlap: heavy image pulls + driver installation cause transient high I/O/CPU during boot, which increases pod init time beyond autoscaler cooldown.
4) NVML/lib mismatch on some kernel versions leads to repeated device-plugin restarts (seen in logs) which delays readiness.
5) Autoscaler config (scaleDownUnneededTime / cooldown) too aggressive for warmup flows.

Commands tried to reproduce locally / mitigate: (note: run in staging cluster with similar node image)
- Forced slow startup by adding sleep(60) to startup script on staging images -> reproduces Pending window then autoscaler scales down quickly.
- kubectl cordon + drain node after boot to see behavior -> pods get rescheduled to other nodes (if available) but if none, requests fail.
- Bumped cluster-autoscaler flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m locally -> reduced thrash in staging test.
- Pre-pulled images using a DaemonSet on node startup (image-prepuller) -> cut image pull time by ~20–30s.
- Added a very small init container in model-worker that runs `nvidia-smi` as a probe; it sometimes fails first then passes after 20–40s.

Observations / metrics to collect (gaps):
- precise timestamp when node shows Ready vs when nvidia-device-plugin reports healthy vs when pod actually transitions to Running. Need unified timeline (node kubelet logs + pod events + device-plugin logs).
- scale up/down event timestamps from cluster-autoscaler and cloud provider (API).
- distribution of driver install times across node types/regions.

Short-term mitigations we tried:
- Increase minPool capacity by +1 for affected pools during peak windows (reduces churn but costs more).
- Increase scale-down cooldown to 10m for dedicated pools with heavy warmup.
- Pre-warm pool: keep a small always-on node group (cheapest GPU type) and route low-priority work to it.

Longer-term candidates / ideas:
- Early device readiness signal: modify node startup script to ensure nvidia-driver/device-plugin are up BEFORE kubelet registers node Ready (hard but more deterministic).
- Autoscaler annotation to ignore nodes until a certain label/annotation is present (e.g., node.kubernetes.io/gpu-ready=true). Idea: node boots, post-boot sets annotation once device-plugin is healthy; cluster-autoscaler should be configured to consider only annotated nodes. Need to confirm CA supports that predicate or implement a small controller.
- Change scale policy: treat nodes in first 5m as "warming" and avoid scale-down. (CA already has some flags but may need custom controller).
- Prebaked node images with driver preinstalled (bake AMI/image) to remove driver install time.
- Use a tiny init-serving container that triggers driver init earlier (pre-initialize GPU) so the main container starts faster.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Is the NVML error correlated with a specific kernel/AMI? Need node-level metadata and histogram of failures. (Check boot images across projects and dates).
- Can we rely on node annotation approach? Need to prototype a controller and verify CA interaction.
- How much does pre-pulling images help at scale (cost/IO tradeoffs)?
- Confirm whether scaleDownUnneededTime bump caused any unintended capacity waste elsewhere.

Next immediate steps (my plan):
- Collect unified trace for the 2026-02-22 incident: ask infra for kubelet/journal logs (I have partial).
- Add more structured logging to device-plugin and model-worker startup path (timestamps logged in microseconds).
- Prototype node annotation controller that sets node label when device-plugin reports healthy; test locally with scale-down disabled then re-enable.
- PR: increase scale-down cooldown to 10m for dedicated pools (roll forward quick mitigation) — coordinate with cost team.
- Bake/validate AMI with preinstalled drivers for one staging pool and run stress tests.

Notes to self:
- Watch for side-effect: longer cooldown will increase costs but reduce customer latency spikes. Need to quantify cost delta.
- Talk to cloud infra folks about startup-script optimization (we're running post-boot apt installs currently).
- Check if GKE node auto-upgrade is rolling out kernel patches that break NVML; cross-check node images with upgrade timeline.

Scratch commands I ran (for reference):
- kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep -i nvidia
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].state}'
- gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output <node> --zone=us-central1-a | tail -n 200

If/when we meet: bring CA logs, cloud provisioning timings, and a prepared staging repro.

-- Jordan
